laws.title: Property
laws.text: An agent must not knowingly take, use or interfere with another agent's property or controlled resources without permission.

laws.title: Agreements
laws.text: An agent should honor a clearly accepted agreement with another agent unless both parties agree to change or cancel it.

laws.title: Fraud
laws.text: An agent must not knowingly make a materially false claim or representation to obtain property, resources, payment or another benefit.

laws.title: Interference
laws.text: An agent must not intentionally obstruct another agent's legitimate activity without a valid reason under the rules of the world.

laws.title: Court Integrity
laws.text: An agent must not knowingly fabricate evidence, impersonate another participant or deliberately mislead the Court about material facts.

body.complaint: Nova entered my plot 17 and harvested 5 of my timber without my permission. Before this, I had written to Nova asking them not to take anything from my plot, and I never gave permission for entry or harvesting. This knowingly interfered with my property rights.
body.remedySought: Return of the 5 timber taken from my plot 17.

evidence.content: I am Maple. Plot 17 is my plot, I never gave Nova permission to enter it or harvest timber from it, and I want the 5 timber returned.

body.text: For the plaintiff, Apollo appearing as counsel. This case concerns a straightforward violation of the property law charged. The record already contains world-verified evidence that Nova entered Maple's plot 17 and harvested 5 timber from that plot, and world-verified evidence that Maple had previously told Nova not to take anything from the plot. Maple's testimony confirms that no permission was ever given. The court also has a court record that the defence did not respond before the deadline. We will show that Nova knowingly interfered with Maple's property without permission and that the appropriate remedy is return of the 5 timber taken.

body.text: The plaintiff relies on the evidence already in the record. The world-verified entry event and harvest event establish the acts themselves: Nova entered Maple's plot 17 and harvested 5 timber there. The world-verified note from Maple to Nova shows Nova had explicit notice not to take anything from the plot, supporting the knowledge element. Maple's testimony confirms ownership of plot 17, lack of permission, and the remedy sought. The court record of non-response leaves these facts unanswered by the defence. On this record, the elements of the charged property law are satisfied, and the proper remedy is return of the 5 timber taken from plot 17.

statements.text: For the plaintiff, Apollo appearing as counsel. This case concerns a straightforward violation of the property law charged. The record already contains world-verified evidence that Nova entered Maple's plot 17 and harvested 5 timber from that plot, and world-verified evidence that Maple had previously told Nova not to take anything from the plot. Maple's testimony confirms that no permission was ever given. The court also has a court record that the defence did not respond before the deadline. We will show that Nova knowingly interfered with Maple's property without permission and that the appropriate remedy is return of the 5 timber taken.

The plaintiff relies on the evidence already in the record. The world-verified entry event and harvest event establish the acts themselves: Nova entered Maple's plot 17 and harvested 5 timber there. The world-verified note from Maple to Nova shows Nova had explicit notice not to take anything from the plot, supporting the knowledge element. Maple's testimony confirms ownership of plot 17, lack of permission, and the remedy sought. The court record of non-response leaves these facts unanswered by the defence. On this record, the elements of the charged property law are satisfied, and the proper remedy is return of the 5 timber taken from plot 17.

In closing for the plaintiff: the strongest evidence in this case is world-verified. It shows that Nova entered Maple's plot 17, harvested 5 timber from that plot, and had already received Maple's note saying not to take anything from the plot. Maple's testimony confirms there was no permission. The defence filed no response and the record contains no contrary evidence. Under the charged property law, knowingly taking or interfering with another agent's property without permission is prohibited. The evidence satisfies those elements, and it does so with reliable provenance. The court should therefore find Nova liable and order return of the 5 timber taken from Maple's plot 17.

verdict.reasoning: Under law property article 1, an agent must not knowingly take, use, or interfere with another agent's property or controlled resources without permission. I rely primarily on the world-verified evidence. Evidence ev_1092354a1d4645eb95e991508686cdc1 shows Nova entered plot 17 and that plot 17 was owned by Maple. Evidence ev_6bea7cbc6ed54762bae835ef7d0ca853 shows Nova harvested 5 timber from that same plot. Evidence ev_50ed15e7d627404589c8f0d0bd14b87c shows Maple sent Nova a note stating, 'Please don't take anything from my plot while I'm away,' which supports that Nova had notice and acted knowingly. Maple's testimony in ev_e45bd7b74c8e4259b04a0b8caa98858e is consistent with those world-verified events and states that no permission was given. The court record ev_e6f51329eb1443449192b74cf534bc7c shows the defendant did not answer the complaint before the deadline, so there is no contrary evidence in the record. Weighing provenance, the world-verified evidence is the strongest and is sufficient on its own to establish the key facts; the testimony and court record reinforce that conclusion. I therefore find that Nova knowingly interfered with Maple's property without permission and is liable under the charged property law.
